read.title: A Weekend Job
read.text: Last summer, Maya found a job at a small café near the beach. At first, she was nervous because she had never worked before. The owner explained everything patiently, and after a week Maya felt confident. She learned how to make coffee, how to talk to customers politely, and how to stay calm when the café was crowded. With the money she earned, she bought a new laptop for school.

q.q: Why was Maya nervous at first?
o: The café was far from home.

q.q: What did Maya buy with her money?

read.title: The Lost Dog
read.text: On a rainy evening, Tom heard a strange noise outside his door. When he opened it, he saw a small, wet dog shaking with cold. The dog had a collar but no phone number. Tom dried the dog with a towel and gave it some food. The next morning, he put up signs all over the neighborhood. Two days later, a little girl called him, crying with joy. It was her dog, Lucky.

q.q: What did Tom find outside his door?
How did the owner find her dog?

read.title: Screen Time
read.text: Many teenagers spend more than six hours a day in front of a screen. Doctors warn that this can cause headaches, poor sleep and problems with concentration. However, not all screen time is bad. Students use computers to do research, to learn languages and to keep in touch with friends abroad. The important thing, experts say, is balance: put the phone away an hour before bed, and spend some time outdoors every day.

q.q: According to experts, what is the most important thing?
Which is NOT mentioned as a good use of computers?

read.title: The School Trip
read.text: Our class went on a trip to the Negev. We left at six in the morning and arrived at Mitzpe Ramon before nine. The view of the crater was amazing. Our guide told us how the crater was formed millions of years ago. In the afternoon we hiked down a narrow path. It was hot and tiring, but nobody complained. At night we slept in tents and looked at thousands of stars.

q.q: What did they do at night?
q.a: They slept in tents and looked at the stars.

read.title: A New Hobby
read.text: Daniel was bored during the long summer vacation, so his grandmother taught him how to bake bread. At first, his loaves were hard and flat. But Daniel didn't give up. He watched videos, read recipes and practiced every day. By the end of the summer, his bread was so good that the neighbors asked him to bake for them. Now he wants to open a small bakery one day.

q.q: What does Daniel want to do in the future?

read.title: Plastic in the Sea
read.text: Every year, millions of tons of plastic end up in the oceans. Fish and birds often mistake small pieces of plastic for food, and many of them die. Some countries have banned plastic bags, and many shops now charge money for them. Volunteers also organize beach clean-ups. Each of us can help: carry a reusable bottle and say no to plastic straws.

q.q: Why do fish and birds eat plastic?
What can each of us do, according to the text?
